newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia bourse to trade five days a week from Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: Latvia bourse to trade five days a week from Feb 3.

text.p: Latvia's bourse said on Friday it would start trading five days a week from the present four from February 3 and soon expects market capitalisation to be higher than the amount of outstanding government T-bills.
Both Latvia's and Lithuania's bourses have seen active trade lately, following the lead of the Estonian bourse.
Shares have become popular as yields on government T-bills have fallen as economic reform and stabilisation takes hold.
"In less than a month we could see the volume of the stock market outgrowing government T-bills, which dominated until now," bourse president Uldis Cerps told a news conference.
The Latvian stock exchange went over to a four-day trading week in December last year and up to now was only missing trade on Mondays.
Current market capitalisation is 112.31 million lats against 16.09 million last April while the current volume of Latvian Treasury bills is some 120 million lats.
